ClientLens

# This website

Last updated: 30 October 2026

**The short version**
clientlens.co is a plain, static website. It sets no cookies, runs no analytics and loads nothing from third parties. The only record of your visit is the standard server log kept by our host, GitHub Pages.

## What this website does not do

- **No cookies.** The site stores nothing in your browser.
- **No analytics.** We do not count visitors, measure clicks or build profiles.
- **No third-party scripts, fonts or embeds.** Every page is made of our own HTML and CSS, using the fonts already on your device. Your browser contacts no other company to show it.
- **No forms and no accounts.** The only way to reach us is by email, which you send from your own mail app.

## Hosting and server logs

The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub, Inc. Like any web host, GitHub keeps standard server logs of visits, which include your IP address and browser type, to keep the service secure and running. GitHub holds these logs under its own policy, not ours; see [GitHub's privacy statement](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement) and its [note on GitHub Pages data collection](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages#data-collection). We do not receive or look at these logs.

## Do Not Track

This website does not track you over time or across other websites, and lets no third party do so. Browser "Do Not Track" and Global Privacy Control signals are therefore treated the same way for everyone: there is no tracking to turn off.

## When you email us

If you write to us, we receive your email address, your message and anything you attach, and we use them only to answer you. How long we keep support emails and what rights you have over them are set out in each app's own privacy policy, which is linked from that app's page.

## The apps

This note covers the website only. Each ClientLens app has its own privacy policy, which describes what that app does with your data. You will find it on the app's page on this site, inside the app, and on its App Store and Google Play listing.

## Changes

If this note changes, the new version will be published on this page with a new date.

## Contact

support@clientlens.co

Source: https://clientlens.co/contacts-backup/

# Contacts Backup, Export, Merge

Back up every contact, every field, in one tap.

App Store · coming soon
Google Play · coming soon

Contacts Backup, Export, Merge is an iPhone and Android app that saves a complete copy of your contacts as a standard vCard file, exports them to Excel or CSV, and cleans up duplicate contacts safely. Use it before switching phones, after a sync mistake, or whenever you want a copy of your address book that you control.

**We never see your contacts.**
No account, no server, no ads, no analytics. The app makes no network connections of its own. Backups are kept in the app on your phone, and are included in your phone's own iCloud or Google backup if you use one.

## What it does

**Back up all your contacts.** Every account at once: iCloud, Gmail, Exchange. Phone numbers, emails, addresses, birthdays, full-size photos, and a count of every field saved.

**Restore with a preview.** See what would come back before anything changes. Restore one contact or many. A fresh backup is always saved first.

**Export contacts to Excel or CSV.** Pick your columns or use ready-made layouts for Google Contacts, Outlook and Mailchimp-style newsletter tools. JSON too.

**Merge duplicate contacts safely.** Review pairs side by side. Only clear matches are merged in bulk, and every merge can be undone.

**Backup history you can read.** Each backup shows what changed since the one before. Compare any two, or bring back a single deleted contact.

**Standard vCard files.** Backups are ordinary .vcf files that any phone, Mac, PC, Gmail or Outlook can import.

## How to back up your iPhone contacts

- Open the app and allow access to contacts.
- Tap **Back Up Now**.
- Choose where to keep the file: in the app, Files, iCloud Drive, Google Drive, AirDrop or Mail.
- Check the report. It counts every phone number, email and photo that was saved, so you know nothing was dropped.

## How to export contacts to Excel or CSV

- Open the **Export** tab and pick Excel or CSV.
- Choose a layout, such as Google Contacts or Outlook, or pick your own columns.
- Check the preview, then tap **Export** and send the file where you need it.

## How to merge duplicate contacts

- Open the **Duplicates** tab and tap **Scan**.
- Review each group side by side and pick the card to keep. Details from the other card are added to it.
- Tap **Merge**. Changed your mind? Tap **Undo all**, or restore the backup saved before the merge.

## Price

**Free.** Back up address books of up to 500 contacts, export name, phone and email, and find duplicates. For example, a phone with 450 contacts backs up free; a phone with 800 needs Pro. Restoring is always free.

**Pro, one payment.** US $4.99, or the local price shown in your store. Unlimited contacts, every export column, merging with undo, compare and full history. No subscription.

## Moving to a new phone?

Follow the [step-by-step guide to transfer contacts to a new phone](https://clientlens.co/contacts-backup/transfer/), with examples for iPhone to Android, Android to iPhone and leaving a job.

## Good to know

On iPhone, Apple only lets apps read contact notes with special permission, so notes are not included in backups on iPhone. Every other field is. Questions? See [help and support](https://clientlens.co/contacts-backup/support/).

Source: https://clientlens.co/contacts-backup/support/

Contacts Backup, Export, Merge

# Help and support

Most answers are below. If yours isn't, write to us and include your phone model. Please don't send contact files; we never need them.

support@clientlens.co

In the app, Settings → Contact support opens an email with your app version already filled in.

## Common questions

**How do I move my contacts to a new phone?** Back up on the old phone, send the file to the new phone (AirDrop, Quick Share, Google Drive or email), open it there with the app, check the preview and tap Restore. Restoring is free. See the [step-by-step guide](https://clientlens.co/contacts-backup/transfer/) for examples, including iPhone to Android.

**What does “address books of up to 500 contacts” mean?** The free version backs up your whole address book when it has 500 contacts or fewer. It can't save just part of a bigger one. For example, a phone with 450 contacts backs up free; a phone with 800 contacts needs Pro, and the app says so before it starts. Restoring a backup is always free, whatever its size.

**Where are my backups stored?** In the app on your phone, listed in History. They are also included in your phone's own iCloud or Google backup if you use one, so they move to a new phone restored from that backup. To keep a separate copy, open a backup and tap Share this backup, then save it to Files, iCloud Drive, Google Drive or send it to yourself.

**How do I restore just one contact?** Open History and tap a backup made before the contact was deleted or changed. Under the comparison, open the Deleted tab and tap Bring back. Or tap Restore from this backup, then Select none, and tick only that contact.

**Will restoring delete anything?** No. Restore only adds contacts that are missing and updates ones that changed. Contacts added after the backup stay. A fresh backup of your current contacts is always saved first, so you can undo a restore from History.

**Why does the app show fewer contacts than cards?** When the same person is saved in more than one account, for example iCloud and Gmail, the Contacts app links those cards and shows one contact. The app shows that same contact count, and mentions how many cards make them up.

**Why aren't my notes in the backup on iPhone?** Apple only lets apps read contact notes with a special permission that is rarely granted. Every other field is backed up. On Android, notes are included.

**Can I undo a merge?** Yes. After merging, tap Undo all. Even later, open History and restore the "Before merge" backup that was saved automatically.

**What does "Possible" mean in Duplicates?** The cards might be the same person but the app is not sure, for example two people called only "Ashley", or a shared office number. Possible matches are never merged in bulk; review each one, then tap Merge or Not a duplicate.

**I bought Pro on another phone. How do I get it back?** Sign in with the same Apple ID or Google account, open Settings in the app and tap Restore purchase.

**How do I get a refund?** Purchases are made through Apple or Google, so they handle refunds. On iPhone, go to reportaproblem.apple.com. On Android, open your order history in Google Play, or use the Google Play Help Center. If a refund is granted, Pro turns off the next time the app checks with the store.

**Are my backups in my Google backup on Android?** Usually, but Google keeps at most 25 MB of data per app in an Android device backup. If the app's backups add up to more than that, Android may leave the app out of your Google backup entirely. For example, ten backups of 1,200 contacts with photos at about 11 MB each come to 110 MB, so none of them would be in the Google backup. The History tab on Android shows how much your backups use. To be safe, open a backup in History, tap Share this backup and save it to Google Drive. On iPhone, iCloud backup has no such per-app limit.

**The backup reminder doesn't arrive.** Check that notifications are allowed for the app in your phone's Settings. In the app, Settings → Remind me to back up shows whether reminders are on and when they arrive.

Contacts Backup, Export, Merge

# Privacy policy

Last updated: 22 October 2026

**The short version**
We never receive your contacts. The app has no account and no server, and makes no network connections of its own. Your contacts stay on your device, in the app's backups, and in your phone's own iCloud or Google backup if you use one. They go anywhere else only when you share a file yourself.

## What the app does with your contacts

With your permission, the app reads the contacts on your device from every account on the phone: names, phone numbers, email addresses, postal addresses, birthdays and other dates, photos, related names, social profiles and similar fields. On Android it also reads contact notes. On iPhone it does not, because Apple only allows that with a special permission the app does not have.

It uses that access only to:

- create backup files (vCard) and exports (CSV, Excel, JSON) that you decide where to save or send;
- show you a preview before restoring contacts from a backup;
- find duplicate contacts and, when you confirm, merge them;
- keep backups inside the app on your phone so you can compare and undo changes.

When you open a .vcf file in the app, for example from Mail or Files, the app reads it on your device to show what it contains and to restore from it if you choose. It is not sent anywhere.

The app changes your contacts only when you confirm a restore, a merge, a deletion of empty cards or a copy between accounts. It saves a backup of your contacts first, every time.

## What leaves your device

**Your phone's own backup.** Like other app data, the app's backups are included in your iCloud or computer backup on iPhone, and in your Google backup on Android, if you have these turned on. They are stored in your own account with Apple or Google, not with us, under their privacy terms. You can turn device backup off in your phone's settings.

Google keeps at most 25 MB of data per app in an Android device backup. If the app's backups add up to more than that, Android may leave the app's data out of your Google backup entirely. For example, ten backups of about 11 MB each come to 110 MB, which is over the limit. To keep a copy off the phone, use **Share this backup** and save it to Google Drive or another place you choose.

**Files you share.** Nothing else leaves your device unless you send it. When you choose a destination such as Files, iCloud Drive, Google Drive, AirDrop, Mail or Quick Share, the file goes to that app or service and its own privacy terms apply. The app makes no network connections of its own, and on Android it does not request internet access. Links in Settings, such as this policy, open in your web browser.

## Analytics, advertising and tracking

None. The app contains no analytics, advertising or crash-reporting tools. If you have turned on crash reports in your phone's settings, Apple or Google may receive them through their own systems; they never include contact data.

## When you email us

If you write to support, we receive what you send: your email address, your message and anything you attach. The app's **Contact support** button adds the app version, your phone's system and the number of contacts, never the contacts themselves. Please don't attach a backup file unless we ask for one.

We use these emails only to answer you and to fix problems you report. Our legal basis is our legitimate interest in answering requests you send us. We keep support emails for up to 24 months after the conversation ends, then delete them. You can ask us to delete them sooner at any time.

Our email is provided by our mail service, which stores messages on our behalf.

## Notifications

If you turn on backup reminders, the app schedules them on your phone. They are not sent from a server.

## Purchases

The one-time Pro purchase is handled by Apple's App Store or Google Play. The app only learns that the purchase exists. We never see your payment details.

## How long data is kept

Backups stay in the app on your device until you delete them in History, until your "Keep backups" setting removes older ones, or until you delete the app. Copies already in your iCloud or Google device backup follow that backup's own retention.

## Children

The app is not directed at children under 13 and collects no data from anyone.

## Your rights

The app collects no data, so for app use we hold nothing to show, correct or delete for you. Everything stays under your control: on your device and in your own device backups.

If you have emailed us, you can ask for a copy of those emails, for corrections, or for their deletion by writing to the address below. We answer within 30 days. If you are unhappy with our answer, you can complain to the data protection authority where you live (in the EU or UK, your national regulator).

Users in India can raise a grievance with our grievance contact at the address below; we acknowledge it within 72 hours and resolve it within 30 days.

## Changes to this policy

If this policy changes, the new version will be published on this page with a new date. Important changes will also be mentioned in the app's release notes.

## Contact

Publisher: ClientLens (company being formed; its registered name and address will be listed here before the app is released).

Privacy and grievance contact: support@clientlens.co

Contacts Backup, Export, Merge

# Terms of use

Last updated: 21 October 2026

**The short version**
You can use the app for your own contacts. Keep your own copies of anything important. Purchases and refunds go through Apple or Google. We do our best, but the app is provided as it is.

## Who these terms are between

These terms are between you and ClientLens, the publisher of Contacts Backup, Export, Merge (the "app"). ClientLens is a company being formed; its registered name and address will be listed here before the app is released. By using the app you agree to these terms. If you got the app from the App Store, Apple's Licensed Application End User License Agreement also applies; if you got it from Google Play, Google Play's terms also apply. Where they differ, the store's terms win for anything about the store.

## Using the app

We give you a personal, non-transferable licence to use the app on devices you own or control, for contacts you are allowed to handle. Please don't copy, resell, or reverse engineer the app except where the law allows it.

## Your contacts and your backups

Your contacts belong to you. The app works on your device, and we never receive them (see the [privacy policy](https://clientlens.co/contacts-backup/privacy/)). You are responsible for where you save or send backup and export files. Backups kept only in the app are lost if you delete the app or lose the phone without a device backup, so keep a copy somewhere else for anything you can't afford to lose: use **Share this backup** to save one to Files, iCloud Drive, Google Drive or your computer.

The app always saves a backup before it changes your contacts, and shows a preview before a restore. Still, check the preview and the results. Contact sync services (iCloud, Google, Exchange) may change contacts after the app writes them, and we can't control that.

## Free and Pro

The free version backs up address books of up to 500 contacts, exports name, phone and email columns, and finds duplicates. Pro is a one-time in-app purchase that removes the limit and unlocks the other features listed in the app. The price is shown in your store before you buy, in your local currency.

Pro is tied to your Apple ID or Google account, not to a ClientLens account. Use **Restore purchase** in the app on a new phone signed in to the same account. On iPhone, Pro can be shared with your Family Sharing group.

## Refunds

Payments are taken by Apple or Google, so refunds are handled by them under their policies. On iPhone, request one at reportaproblem.apple.com. On Android, use Google Play's order history or the Google Play Help Center. If a refund is granted, Pro is turned off the next time the app checks with the store. Nothing in these terms takes away refund or withdrawal rights you have under the law where you live.

## Changes to the app

We may update the app to fix problems, follow store rules, or add features. If we ever stop offering the app, a Pro purchase you already made keeps working on the version you have.

## No warranty

We work hard to make the app reliable, but it is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any kind, to the extent the law allows. We don't promise it will be error-free or that every field of every contact can be read or written on every phone; for example, iPhone does not let apps read contact notes.

## Limit of liability

To the extent the law allows, ClientLens is not liable for indirect or consequential losses, or for loss of data you could have avoided by keeping your own backup copy. Our total liability for any claim about the app is limited to the amount you paid for it in the 12 months before the claim. Some places don't allow these limits, so they may not apply to you; your statutory consumer rights are not affected.

## Governing law

These terms are governed by the law of the place where ClientLens is registered, which will be stated here once the company is formed. If you are a consumer, you also keep the protection of the mandatory laws of the country where you live, and you can bring a claim in your local courts.

## Changes to these terms

If these terms change, the new version will be published on this page with a new date. Important changes will also be mentioned in the app's release notes.

## Contact

support@clientlens.co

Contacts Backup, Export, Merge

# Accessibility

Last updated: 21 October 2026

**Our goal**
Everyone should be able to back up, restore, export and merge their contacts. We aim for the app to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA on iPhone and Android.

## What the app supports

- **VoiceOver and TalkBack.** Buttons, toggles, checkboxes and choices are labelled and report their state, such as "checked" or "selected". Screen titles are announced as headings.
- **Spoken progress.** Backups, merges and restores announce their progress and results, so you don't need to watch the screen.
- **Larger text.** Text follows your phone's text size setting. Lists and buttons grow to fit instead of cutting words off. Tab labels grow up to one and a half times.
- **Colour and contrast.** Text and controls meet AA contrast. Information shown in colour, such as a field that will be added during a merge, is also given in words.
- **Touch targets.** Buttons and links are at least 44 by 44 points.
- **Any orientation.** The app works in portrait and landscape, including on iPad.
- **No time limits and no flashing content.**

## Known limits

- The app uses a light appearance only, even when the phone is set to dark mode.
- Very large text sizes can make the comparison of two backups long to scroll; the content stays readable.

## How we test

Before each release we go through backup, restore, export and merge with VoiceOver on iPhone and TalkBack on Android, at default and at the largest text size, and check colour contrast against WCAG 2.2.

## Tell us about a problem

If something in the app or on this website is hard to use with your setup, please write to us and say what you were trying to do and which phone and assistive technology you use. We aim to reply within 5 working days.

support@clientlens.co

Contacts Backup, Export, Merge

# Transfer contacts to a new phone

Last updated: 22 October 2026

**The short version**
Make a backup on the old phone, send the file to the new phone, open it there with the app, check the preview, and tap Restore. Nothing is uploaded to us at any step.

## Before you start

- **Install the app on the old phone.** That is where the backup is made.
- **Check the size of your address book.** The free version backs up address books of up to 500 contacts. For example, a phone with 450 contacts is free; a phone with 800 contacts needs Pro on the old phone to make the backup. The app tells you before you start.
- **Restoring is always free**, whatever the size, so the new phone never needs Pro just to bring contacts in.
- **Already synced?** If all your contacts are in iCloud (iPhone to iPhone) or in your Google account (Android to Android), signing in on the new phone may bring them across on its own. A backup is still the safest way to make sure nothing is missed, and it is the only way across between iPhone and Android, or for contacts saved only "On My iPhone" or on the phone itself.

## Step by step

- **Back up the old phone.** Open the app and tap **Back Up Now**. Wait for the report; it counts the phone numbers, emails and photos that were saved.
- **Send the backup file to the new phone.** Under **Save to**, pick the easiest way:
  - **AirDrop**: iPhone to iPhone, when both phones are next to each other.
  - **Quick Share**: Android to Android.
  - **Files**: save to iCloud Drive or Google Drive, then open it on the new phone. Works between iPhone and Android.
  - **Mail**: email it to yourself. Fine for small address books; a book with many photos may be too big to attach.
- **Open the file on the new phone.** Install the app on the new phone. Tap **Restore from a backup** (on Android, **Restore**), then **Browse Files** and pick the .vcf file. Or tap the file in AirDrop, Mail or Drive and choose the app.
- **Check the preview.** It shows how many contacts will be added and which ones already match. Untick anyone you don't want to bring.
- **Pick where they go.** Under **Add them back to**, choose the account that should keep them, usually iCloud on iPhone or your Google account on Android, so they also sync to your other devices.
- **Tap Restore.** The new phone's current contacts are backed up first, so you can undo from **History** if something looks wrong.

## Examples

### iPhone to iPhone

Maya has 320 contacts on her old iPhone, some saved only "On My iPhone". She taps **Back Up Now**, chooses **AirDrop** and sends the file to her new iPhone. On the new iPhone she taps the file, chooses the app, picks **iCloud** under **Add them back to** and taps **Restore 320 contacts**. All 320 are now in iCloud, including the ones that were never synced before.

### iPhone to Android

Arjun is moving from an iPhone with 640 contacts to an Android phone. 640 is over the free limit, so he unlocks Pro on the iPhone and taps **Back Up Now**, then **Files**, and saves the file to Google Drive. On the Android phone he installs the app (restoring is free), taps **Restore**, **Browse files**, and picks the file from Drive. He chooses his Google account so the contacts also appear in Gmail, and taps **Restore**.

### Android to iPhone

Lena's Android phone has 410 contacts. Quick Share doesn't reach an iPhone, so she chooses **Files** and saves the backup to Google Drive (or emails it to herself with **Gmail**). On the iPhone she opens the file from the Drive app or Mail, chooses the app, picks **iCloud** and restores.

### Leaving a job: work contacts to your own account

Sam's work Exchange account holds 150 contacts that will disappear when the employer removes the account. In the app, Sam taps the accounts line on Home (or Settings, then Accounts and groups). The work account shows how many contacts exist only there, with a button to copy them to the personal account. Contacts already saved in both places are not copied twice. Do this before your last day.

## Without the app on the new phone

A backup is an ordinary .vcf file, so the new phone can also import it directly. You won't get the preview or the duplicate check, so contacts that are already on the new phone may appear twice.

- **iPhone:** tap the .vcf file in Files, Mail or Messages, then tap **Add All Contacts**.
- **Android:** in the Contacts app, open **Fix & manage** and choose **Import from file**, then pick the .vcf file.

If you end up with duplicates, the app's **Duplicates** tab finds them and lets you merge them, with undo.

## Good to know

- **Notes on iPhone:** Apple doesn't let apps read contact notes, so a backup made on an iPhone doesn't include them. Backups made on Android do.
- **Keep the old phone until you've checked.** Open a few contacts on the new phone, including some with photos, before you reset the old one.
- **Keep a copy.** Save one backup to iCloud Drive, Google Drive or your computer. It is useful the next time you change phones too.

Stuck? See [help and support](https://clientlens.co/contacts-backup/support/).

Source: https://clientlens.co/printcal/

# PrintCal: Print Your Calendar

Print the calendar already on your phone.

App Store · coming soon
Google Play · coming soon

Planned for early December 2026, in time to print next year's calendar.

PrintCal is an iPhone, iPad and Android app that prints the calendars you already have (iCloud, Google, Outlook, Exchange and any other calendar on the phone) as clean, readable pages. Pick a month, a week or a list, then print with AirPrint or the Android print service, or save a PDF. The iPhone Calendar app and the Google Calendar app have no print button; PrintCal is that button.

**Nothing leaves your phone.**
No account, no ads, no analytics, no internet access. PrintCal reads your calendars on the phone and never changes them. App Store privacy label: Data Not Collected. Google Play Data safety: no data collected or shared.

## Made for paper

**Every event prints.** When a day is full, the extra events continue on an overflow page instead of being cut off. Nothing is dropped silently.

**Readable from across the kitchen.** Auto-fit grows text to fill the space, plus bold and a Large Print preset. Day numbers you can read from the door.

**The right paper.** Letter or A4 picked for your region, portrait or landscape, with printer-safe margins. The preview is the page that prints.

**Your details, your choice.** Start and end times, location, notes, calendar name. Hide holidays and birthdays. Weekdays only for a work schedule.

**All your calendars.** Each calendar in its own colour with a legend. Your selection is saved, so the fridge calendar is one tap next month.

**Multi-day events done right.** A trip prints as one bar across the days, split cleanly at the week row. Meetings sit at their exact minutes in week view.

## How to print your calendar from your phone

- Open PrintCal and allow calendar access. Access is read-only; the app never adds, changes or deletes an event.
- Your current month appears already laid out. Switch to **Week** or **List** if you prefer, and tick the calendars to include.
- Adjust **Style** if you like: text size, bold or Large Print, details, paper.
- Tap **Print** to use your phone's print dialog (AirPrint or the Android print service), or **Share** to save a PDF to Files, Google Drive or Downloads.

Step-by-step guides with the built-in options too: [how to print your iPhone calendar](https://clientlens.co/printcal/print-iphone-calendar/) and [how to print Google Calendar from your phone](https://clientlens.co/printcal/print-google-calendar/).

## Free and Pro

**Free.** Month, week and list views. All your calendars and real events, with saved selections. Event details, text size, bold, Large Print and auto-fit. Week start, weekdays only, day hours. Letter and A4. One month or one week at a time, "This month" and "This week" quick print, one saved preset, and a small footer line on the page. Free output is never blocked or watermarked.

**Pro, one purchase.** Day view and Year view (one poster or 12 pages). Any date range, up to 24 months in one PDF, past and future years. Custom title, mini months and a notes column. Four print fonts with separate sizes. Custom colours per calendar. Legal, Tabloid, A3, A5 and poster sizes. Unlimited presets and no footer line. On iPhone: Reminders lists as checklists, home-screen quick actions and Shortcuts links, and Family Sharing. On Android: home-screen app shortcuts. The price is shown in your store, in your currency. No subscription.

## Good to know

- The app is in English, Spanish, German, French, Portuguese (Brazil) and Japanese. Month and weekday names on the page follow your phone's language; the page's own small labels (such as "All day") are in English in this release.
- PrintCal prints the calendars your phone's Calendar app shows. A calendar switched off there is hidden from every app, including this one.
- Reminders printing is available on iPhone and iPad only; Android has no Reminders.

Questions? See [help and support](https://clientlens.co/printcal/support/).

Source: https://clientlens.co/printcal/print-iphone-calendar/

PrintCal: Print Your Calendar

# How to print your iPhone calendar

Last updated: 29 October 2026

**The short version**
The Calendar app on iPhone and iPad has no Print command. You can print the same calendars from a Mac, make do with a screenshot, or use an app on the phone that prints. Below, each way with its trade-offs, built-in options first.

## Why there is no print button

Apple's Calendar app on iPhone and iPad can share an event, but it cannot print a month, a week or a list. The Google Calendar and Outlook apps on iPhone can't either. Your events are still there in iCloud (or in your Google or Outlook account), so the question is just which screen you print them from.

## Option 1: Print from a Mac (built in, free)

If you have a Mac signed in to the same Apple Account, the Mac's Calendar app shows the same iCloud calendars, and it can print.

- On the Mac, open **Calendar**. Check that the calendars you want are ticked in the sidebar.
- Choose **File → Print** (or press ⌘P).
- In the dialog, pick a **View** (Day, Week, Month or List), the **Paper** size, the **Time range**, and which **Calendars** to include. Under Options you can turn on all-day events, timed events, mini months and a calendar key.
- Click **Continue**, then choose a printer or **Save as PDF**.

**Good for:** a quick month or week when a Mac is nearby. **Watch for:** on a full month the text gets very small and events are cut short; there is no large-print setting. Google or Outlook calendars appear only if they are added to the Mac too (System Settings → Internet Accounts).

## Option 2: iCloud.com in a web browser

On any computer, sign in at **icloud.com** and open **Calendar**. There is no Print command of its own, but the browser's Print (⌘P or Ctrl+P) prints the month as it looks on screen.

**Good for:** a computer that isn't a Mac. **Watch for:** the result is a screen print: small text, events shortened, and sometimes the right-hand days cut off. Switch the browser to landscape and "Fit to page" before printing.

## Option 3: A screenshot from the phone

- In Calendar, open the month view. On recent iOS versions, tap the view button at the top and choose **Details** (or **Stacked**) so the month shows event titles rather than dots.
- Take a screenshot (side button + volume up).
- Open it in Photos, tap Share, then **Print**, and choose your AirPrint printer.

**Good for:** a one-off reminder on the fridge. **Watch for:** it is a photo of the screen, so a tall phone shape on Letter paper, small text, and only the events that fit on the screen. Times and locations are not included.

## Option 4: Print straight from the phone with PrintCal

[PrintCal](https://clientlens.co/printcal/) reads the calendars already on your iPhone or iPad (iCloud, Google, Outlook, Exchange, subscribed and shared) and lays them out as a proper page.

- Open PrintCal and allow calendar access. Choose **Full Access**; write-only access cannot read events. Access is read-only: the app never changes an event.
- The current month appears already laid out. Switch to **Week** or **List** if you prefer, and tick the calendars to include in the **Calendars** sheet.
- In **Style**, choose text size, bold or **Large Print**, which details to show (end times, location, notes), and Letter or A4.
- Tap **Print** to send the page to an AirPrint printer through the iPhone's print dialog, or **Share** to save a PDF to Files or iCloud Drive, or send it by Mail.

**Good for:** a readable month or week with every event on it, when there is no Mac around, or when the people reading it need big text. When a day is too full, the extra events go on an overflow page instead of being cut off. **Watch for:** like any app, it can only see calendars that are turned on in the Calendar app; a calendar hidden under Calendar → Calendars is hidden from PrintCal too. Month, week and list are free; day and year pages are part of the one-time Pro purchase.

## Which one should I use?

- You want: Use
- A quick month, Mac nearby: Option 1, Mac Calendar
- A Windows PC and iCloud calendars: Option 2, iCloud.com, or Option 4 from the phone
- A one-off note on the fridge, right now: Option 3, screenshot
- Big text, every event, from the phone, PDF or paper: Option 4, PrintCal
- A Google calendar you use on your iPhone: See [how to print Google Calendar](https://clientlens.co/printcal/print-google-calendar/)

## Good to know

- **No printer?** Every option above can save a PDF instead; print it later from a computer or a print shop.
- **Letter or A4.** Pick the same paper size in the print dialog that the page was made for, or the printer will shrink or crop it.
- **Next year's calendar.** Calendar on the Mac can print any date range. In PrintCal, the free version prints one month or one week at a time; printing a whole year, past or future, is part of Pro.

Stuck? See [help and support](https://clientlens.co/printcal/support/).

---

Source: https://clientlens.co/printcal/print-google-calendar/

PrintCal: Print Your Calendar

# How to print Google Calendar from your phone

Last updated: 29 October 2026

**The short version**
The Google Calendar app on Android and iPhone has no print button. The Google Calendar website does, so you can print from a computer, or from your phone's browser in desktop mode. For a page made for paper, with every event and big text, an app on the phone such as PrintCal prints the same calendar directly.

## Option 1: The Google Calendar website on a computer (built in, free)

- Go to **calendar.google.com** and sign in.
- Pick the view at the top right: **Month**, **Week**, **Day** or **Schedule**. Tick the calendars to include in the list on the left.
- Click the **Settings** gear and choose **Print**.
- Set the **date range**, **font size**, **orientation**, colour or black and white, and whether to show events you declined. The preview updates as you go.
- Click **Print**, then choose a printer or **Save as PDF** in the browser's print dialog.

**Good for:** anyone with a computer; it's free and it's Google's own layout. **Watch for:** a month page shows titles only, and a busy day shows "+N more" with the rest left off the page. To print event details, switch to **Schedule** view first: it prints each event with its time, one line after another, though without the grid. Larger font sizes make a month spill onto more pages.

## Option 2: The same website, from your phone's browser

The website works on a phone too, if you ask for the desktop version.

- Open **calendar.google.com** in your browser (not the app). If it opens the app or a simple mobile page, go back to the browser tab.
- Switch to desktop mode. **Chrome (Android and iPhone):** the ⋮ menu → **Desktop site**. **Safari (iPhone):** the **aA** button in the address bar → **Request Desktop Website**.
- Follow the steps of Option 1: Settings gear → Print → set the options → Print. In the phone's print dialog, choose a printer or **Save as PDF**.

**Good for:** an emergency when no computer is near. **Watch for:** the desktop page is tiny on a phone and the Print dialog is fiddly; zoom in to reach the controls. The result is the same as Option 1.

## Option 3: Print straight from the phone with PrintCal

[PrintCal](https://clientlens.co/printcal/) reads the calendars synced to your phone, including Google Calendar, and lays them out as a page made for paper: big text, every event, a legend for your calendars.

### On Android

- Make sure your Google account syncs its calendar: Android Settings → Accounts (or Passwords & accounts) → your Google account → **Calendar** sync on. If the calendar is ticked in the Google Calendar app, it is available to PrintCal.
- Open PrintCal and **Allow** calendar access. Access is read-only; the app never changes an event and has no internet access.
- The current month appears. Tick the Google calendars you want in the **Calendars** sheet. Switch to **Week** or **List** if you prefer.
- In **Style**, choose text size, bold or **Large Print**, details (end times, location, notes) and the paper size.
- Tap **Print** to use Android's print service (most Wi-Fi printers), or **Share** to save a PDF to Google Drive or Downloads.

### On iPhone or iPad

- Add your Google account to the iPhone's calendars if it isn't already: Settings → Apps → Calendar → **Calendar Accounts** → Add Account → Google, with Calendars turned on. (On older iOS versions: Settings → Calendar → Accounts.) Your Google events then appear in the iPhone Calendar app.
- Open PrintCal and allow calendar access, choosing **Full Access**.
- Tick the Google calendars in the **Calendars** sheet, set **Style**, then **Print** with AirPrint or **Share** a PDF.

**Good for:** a fridge or door calendar you can read from across the room, a work week with exact times, a list with notes and locations, all from the phone. When a day is too full for the grid, the extra events continue on an overflow page instead of being left off. **Watch for:** PrintCal shows the calendars your phone's calendar app shows; a Google calendar unticked in Google Calendar, or an account with calendar sync off, is hidden from every app. Month, week and list are free; day and year pages are part of the one-time Pro purchase.

## Which one should I use?

- You want: Use
- A quick month from a computer: Option 1, the website
- Times and details for every event, from a computer: Option 1 in Schedule view
- No computer, once in a while: Option 2, desktop mode in the phone's browser
- A readable page with every event, from the phone, paper or PDF: Option 3, PrintCal
- iCloud calendars on an iPhone: See [how to print your iPhone calendar](https://clientlens.co/printcal/print-iphone-calendar/)

## Good to know

- **Google Tasks** are not part of a calendar's events, so none of these options prints them as calendar entries. Open Google Tasks itself for a list.
- **Holidays and birthdays** come from their own calendars. Untick them before printing if they crowd the page; in PrintCal they have their own switches.
- **Letter or A4.** Pick the same paper size in the print dialog that the page was made for, or the printer will shrink or crop it.

Stuck? See [help and support](https://clientlens.co/printcal/support/).

---

Source: https://clientlens.co/printcal/support/

PrintCal: Print Your Calendar

# Help and support

Most answers are below. If yours isn't, write to us and say which phone you have and what you were trying to print. Please don't send your calendar; we never need it.

support@clientlens.co

In the app, Settings → Contact support opens an email with your app version and phone model already filled in. You can read and edit it before sending.

## Calendar access

**Why can't the app see my calendar?** PrintCal reads calendars only with your permission, and the page stays blank until it has it. On iPhone, turn it on under Settings → Apps → PrintCal → Calendars → **Full Access**. On Android, Settings → Apps → PrintCal → Permissions → Calendar → **Allow**. Come back to the app and it re-checks on its own, no restart needed. Settings → Calendar access in the app shows what it can see right now.

**What is "limited" or "add events only" access on iPhone?** iOS can give an app write-only access: the app may add events but cannot read any. Printing needs to read, so it needs full access. Open Settings → Apps → PrintCal → Calendars and choose **Full Access**.

**Does the app change my events?** No. Access is used to read only; PrintCal never adds, edits or deletes an event, and never sends one anywhere.

**A calendar I use is not in the list** PrintCal lists the calendars your phone's calendar app shows. On iPhone, a calendar that is off under Calendar → Calendars is hidden from every app; turn it on there and it appears in PrintCal. Subscribed and shared calendars show too, once iOS has downloaded them. On Android, a calendar you have unticked in Google Calendar or Samsung Calendar is hidden the same way; tick it there, and check Settings → Accounts → the account → Calendar sync is on.

**The calendar is there but the month is empty** Open the **Calendars** sheet on the page and check that the calendar is ticked. Holidays switch off by themselves when a month has more than ten of them; turn them back on in the same sheet.

## Pages, printers and paper

**A day was full. Where did the rest of its events go?** On an overflow page right after the month, grouped by date. The day's cell shows "+N more" so you know to look there. Nothing is dropped. If you would rather have everything in the grid, choose a smaller text size, hide some details, or print the week instead.

**Which printers work?** Any printer your phone can print to: AirPrint printers on iPhone and iPad, and any printer set up in Android's print service. Print opens the phone's own print dialog, so the choice of printer, copies and double-sided is made there. With no printer nearby, choose Save as PDF and print the file from a computer.

**Letter or A4?** PrintCal picks the paper from your region: Letter in the US, Canada, Mexico and the Philippines, A4 everywhere else. Change it in **Style** on the page, or set a default under Settings → Defaults → Paper. The page is laid out for that size, so pick the same size in the print dialog.

**The print is small or cut off** Check that the paper in the print dialog matches the page (Letter or A4) and that scaling is 100% or Fit. The page keeps its own margin, so borderless printing is not needed.

**Where does the PDF go?** Tap **Share** and choose where: Files or iCloud Drive on iPhone, Google Drive or Downloads on Android, or any app that accepts a PDF, such as Mail. The file is named after what it holds, for example "Calendar 2027-01 Month.pdf". The app keeps the PDF only in a temporary folder that is emptied at the next launch, so save a copy where you want it.

**Is the printed page in my language?** The app is in English, Spanish, German, French, Portuguese (Brazil) and Japanese and follows your phone's language. Month and weekday names on the page follow it too. The page's own small labels, such as "All day" and "+N more", are in English in this release.

## Free, Pro and purchases

**What is free and what is Pro?** **Free:** month, week and list views, all your calendars and real events with saved selections, event details, text size, bold, Large Print and auto-fit, week start, weekdays only, day hours, Letter and A4, one month or one week at a time, one saved preset and a small footer line on the page. **Pro, one purchase:** day view and year view, any date range up to 24 months in one PDF, custom title, mini months and a notes column, four print fonts with separate sizes, custom calendar colours, Legal, Tabloid, A3, A5 and poster sizes, unlimited presets and no footer line; on iPhone also Reminders checklists, home-screen quick actions and Shortcuts; on Android, home-screen app shortcuts. The price is shown in your store. No subscription.

**I bought Pro. How do I get it on a family member's iPhone?** Pro is one purchase on your App Store account, shared through Family Sharing. On the family member's device open Settings → **Restore purchase** in the app; the App Store finds the purchase through the family. If it says nothing was found, check iPhone Settings → Family → the buyer → Share Purchases with Family.

**And on Android?** Pro belongs to the Google account that bought it and works on every device signed in to that account. Sign in with it, open Settings → **Restore purchase** in the app, and Pro turns on.

**Restore says no purchase was found** Make sure the device is signed in to the account (or family) that bought Pro, then tap **Restore purchase** again. Purchases on the App Store and Google Play are separate: Pro bought on an iPhone does not unlock an Android phone, and the other way round.

**How do I get a refund?** Purchases are made through Apple or Google, so they handle refunds. On iPhone, go to reportaproblem.apple.com. On Android, open your order history in Google Play, or use the Google Play Help Center. If a refund is granted, Pro turns off the next time the app checks with the store.

## Guides

[How to print your iPhone calendar](https://clientlens.co/printcal/print-iphone-calendar/), including the built-in ways from a Mac, and [how to print Google Calendar from your phone](https://clientlens.co/printcal/print-google-calendar/), including the free way through the Google Calendar website.

PrintCal: Print Your Calendar

# Privacy policy

Last updated: 30 October 2026

**The short version**
Nothing leaves your phone. PrintCal has no account, no server, no analytics, no ads and no internet access of its own. It reads your calendars on the phone to lay them out on a page, and never changes them. Its App Store privacy label and Google Play Data safety form both say: no data collected.

## What the app reads

With your permission, the app reads the calendars on your phone: every calendar your Calendar app shows, such as iCloud, Google, Outlook or Exchange, subscribed, shared and local calendars, birthdays and holidays. On iPhone and iPad, with a separate permission, it can also read your Reminders lists (a Pro feature). It uses that access only to lay out your events on the page you asked for.

The reading happens on the phone. Events are kept in memory only while a page is built and are never written to storage or to logs. Access is read-only: PrintCal never adds, edits or deletes an event or a reminder. On Android, the app does not even request the permission that would allow writing.

## What the app keeps

Only your choices: paper size, view, style, which calendars are ticked, your presets and the names you give them, the custom page title you type, how many times you have printed, the date you first opened the app, the date the app last asked you for a rating, and the code of the last error. These are stored in the app's settings file on the device only. Never an event's title, place, notes or link.

The PDF you print or share is written to a temporary folder on the phone that is emptied the next time the app starts. Print, Share and Save hand it only to the phone's print dialog or to the app you pick, such as Files, Google Drive or Mail; that app's own privacy terms then apply.

On iPhone and iPad, these settings are part of your device's own iCloud or computer backup, like any other app's data; they hold no events. On Android, the app opts out of Google device backup, so nothing of it is backed up.

## What the app sends

Nothing. The app has no internet access of its own: on Android it blocks the internet permission entirely, and on iPhone it makes no network connections. It contains no analytics, advertising, attribution or crash-reporting tools. If you have turned on crash or analytics sharing in your phone's settings, Apple or Google may receive reports through their own systems; those never include calendar data.

Links in Settings, such as this policy, open in your web browser. The browser, not the app, makes that connection.

## Do Not Track

Neither the app nor this website tracks you over time or across other websites or apps, and neither lets any third party do so. Browser "Do Not Track" and Global Privacy Control signals are therefore treated the same way for everyone: there is no tracking to turn off. (California's online privacy law, CalOPPA, asks us to say this plainly.)

## Purchases

Pro is a one-time purchase handled by Apple's App Store or Google Play. The store takes the payment and keeps the receipt; the app only asks the store on the phone whether Pro is owned, so that it works on every device signed in to the same account or, on iPhone, the same Family Sharing group. We never see your payment details, and there is no ClientLens server involved.

## When you email us

If you write to support, we receive what you send: your email address, your message and anything you attach. The app's **Contact support** button prepares an email with the app version, your phone's system and model, the number of calendars the app can see and the code of the last error. You see the whole email and can edit it before it is sent from your own mail app. It never includes an event.

We use these emails only to answer you and to fix problems you report. Our legal basis is our legitimate interest in answering requests you send us. We keep support emails for up to 24 months after the conversation ends, then delete them. You can ask us to delete them sooner at any time.

Our email is handled by our email provider, which stores messages on our behalf.

## Notifications

The app sends no notifications.

## How long data is kept

Your settings stay on the phone until you change them or delete the app. Deleting the app removes them. PDFs in the temporary folder are removed at the next launch; copies you saved or shared elsewhere are under your control.

## Children

The app is not directed at children under 13 and collects no data from anyone.

## Your rights

The app collects no data, so for app use we hold nothing to show, correct or delete for you. Everything stays under your control, on your phone.

If you have emailed us, you can ask for a copy of those emails, for corrections, or for their deletion, and you can object to our use of them, by writing to the address below. We answer within 30 days. If you are unhappy with our answer, you can complain to the data protection authority where you live (in the EU or UK, your national regulator).

Users in India can raise a grievance with our grievance contact at the address below; we acknowledge it within 72 hours and resolve it within 30 days.

## Changes to this policy

If this policy changes, the new version will be published on this page with a new date. Important changes will also be mentioned in the app's release notes.

## Contact

Publisher: ClientLens (company being formed; its registered name and address will be listed here before the app is released).

Privacy and grievance contact: support@clientlens.co

Source: https://clientlens.co/printcal/terms/

Your calendars belong to you. The app reads them on your device and never changes them, and we never receive them (see the [privacy policy](https://clientlens.co/printcal/privacy/)). You are responsible for where you print, save or send the pages and PDFs you make, and for who sees them. A printed calendar is a copy made at that moment: events you change afterwards are not updated on paper, so print again when something important moves.

The preview shows the page that will print, and the app is built so that every event in the chosen range appears on a page. Still, check the page before you rely on it, for example before handing a schedule to someone else.

Our total liability for any claim about the app is limited to the amount you paid for it in the 12 months before the claim. Some places don't allow these limits, so they may not apply to you; your statutory consumer rights are not affected.

## Governing law

PrintCal: Print Your Calendar

# Accessibility

Last updated: 30 October 2026

**Our goal**
Everyone should be able to print their calendar, and the printed page should be readable by the people it is for. We aim for the app to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA on iPhone and Android.

## The app

- **VoiceOver and TalkBack.** Buttons, toggles, checkboxes and choices are labelled and report their state, such as "checked" or "selected". Screen titles are announced as headings. On iPhone, error messages are read out by VoiceOver when they appear.
- **Larger text.** The app's own text follows your phone's text size setting, and screens, including the Pro screen, scroll to fit. A few small labels, such as the toolbar and the page counter, may be shortened at the largest sizes.
- **Colour and contrast.** Text and controls meet AA contrast. Nothing is shown by colour alone: a calendar's colour always has a name next to it.
- **Touch targets.** Buttons and links are at least 44 × 44 points.
- **No animation.** The preview has no animations; it simply redraws when you change a setting.
- **Any orientation.** The app works in portrait and landscape, including on iPad.
- **No time limits and no flashing content.**

## The printed page

- **Large Print preset.** One tap sets event text to 16 pt bold and day numbers to 22 pt, in black on white, using Atkinson Hyperlegible, a typeface designed for readers with low vision.
- **Text size and bold.** Four sizes with a live preview, and auto-fit, which grows text to fill the space a light month leaves free.
- **Black-and-white printing.** Calendars are told apart by outline, solid and hatched styles and by their initial, with a legend, so a mono printer or a reader who cannot tell colours apart loses nothing.
- **No event is dropped.** When a day is full, events continue on an extra page (on by default). A title too long for its space ends with "…".

## Known limits

- Screen readers can't yet read the page preview itself; the events are read in your phone's calendar app. An accessible list of the events on the page is planned.
- The app uses a light appearance only, even when the phone is set to dark mode. The paper in the preview is white, as it will print.
- The page preview does not grow with your phone's text size, because it shows the page at its printed proportions. Pinch to zoom in on it, or change the page's own text size in Style.
- The PDF is a printed layout. It is not a tagged PDF, so screen readers on a computer may not read it in order.
- The page's own small labels, such as "All day" and "+N more", are in English in this release.

## How we test

Before launch we will go through calendar access, the month, week and list pages, Style and Print with VoiceOver on iPhone and TalkBack on Android, at default and at the largest text size, and check colour contrast against WCAG 2.2. This page will list the date of each check once it has been done.

- **29 October 2026:** review of the app's labels, roles, state announcements, text sizes and touch targets. This was a code review, not a VoiceOver or TalkBack pass.
- **VoiceOver on iPhone:** before launch (date to be added here).
- **TalkBack on Android:** before launch (date to be added here).
- **Largest text sizes on both:** before launch (date to be added here).

## Tell us about a problem

If something in the app, on a printed page or on this website is hard to use with your setup, please write to us and say what you were trying to do and which phone and assistive technology you use. We aim to reply within 5 working days.

support@clientlens.co
